stories.title: AIIMS Delhi performs first open fetal surgery for spinal defect
stories.summary: AIIMS New Delhi has performed India's first open fetal surgery to repair a lumbosacral myelomeningocele in an unborn baby at 25 weeks gestation. The six-hour procedure followed five weeks of multidisciplinary planning, imaging, and operative simulation. The defect was repaired while the fetus remained in utero.

stories.title: Regenerated bone continues maturing after shape restoration
stories.summary: Regeneration is often measured by visual restoration of missing tissue. A new Texas A&M study indicates that bone may continue to mature mechanically beneath the surface even after it appears whole. The appearance of completion does not necessarily signal the end of the biological process.

stories.title: Alzheimer's blood marker may predict cognitive risk
stories.summary: A blood biomarker for Alzheimer's disease may help estimate a person's risk of developing mild cognitive impairment or dementia over the next five to 10 years. The findings, published in JAMA Neurology, suggest a potential window for early assessment of cognitive health.

stories.title: Kidney protein identified as blood vessel protector
stories.summary: Elevated blood phosphate levels can cause blood vessels to stiffen, increasing cardiovascular risk. A newly identified protein may help protect vessels from this damage. While hyperphosphatemia is rare in the general population, it is widespread among people living with chronic kidney disease.

stories.title: New tool aims to predict T cell behavior
stories.summary: T cells are the immune system's primary tools for cancer immunotherapy, yet their behavior remains difficult to predict. Some cells remain aimless while others activate. A new tool seeks to address this inconsistency, which researchers identify as a primary reason many immunotherapies fail to work.

stories.title: Algorithm predicts brain surgery outcomes in dystonia
stories.summary: Deep brain stimulation is a treatment for dystonia, yet fewer than 5% of patients undergo the procedure. Outcomes vary widely and objective markers for success are lacking. A new algorithm aims to predict surgical results to help identify which patients might benefit from the intervention.

stories.title: Brain connectivity linked to multiple sclerosis damage
stories.summary: Multiple sclerosis involves the immune system attacking myelin, the protective coating around nerve fibers. Research suggests that brain connectivity in high-traffic regions may influence how the disease damages tissue. The damage extends beyond the initial attack on myelin to affect broader communication pathways.

stories.title: Review proposes framework for endometriosis pain treatment
stories.summary: A joint research team has examined how pain develops and persists in patients with endometriosis. The researchers proposed new directions to translate these insights into personalized treatment plans. The review aims to move beyond generalized approaches to address the specific mechanisms of pain in individual patients.

stories.title: New pill combination approved for advanced breast cancer
stories.summary: Patients with advanced breast cancer that has stopped responding to hormone therapy now have a new pill-based treatment option. The approval provides an alternative for those whose disease has progressed despite standard hormonal interventions.

stories.title: Experimental blood cancer immunotherapy reduces death risk
stories.summary: Sellas Life Sciences reported that its experimental immunotherapy, galinpepimut-S, reduced the risk of death in a clinical trial for blood cancer. The company's announcement follows previous skepticism regarding the drug's efficacy in treating the condition.

stories.title: Researchers report progress following gene therapy death
stories.summary: Researchers presented investigations into a gene therapy death that occurred last year. While the specific cause remains under study, the team proposed a framework for screening future therapies. The goal is to mitigate and predict novel risks before they manifest in clinical trials.

stories.title: Diabetes linked to higher Alzheimer's risk
stories.summary: A review of 40 studies found that people with type 2 diabetes face a 53% higher risk of developing Alzheimer's disease. Researchers estimate that for every 1,000 people with diabetes, 4.7 may develop the disorder annually. They suggest integrating cognitive risk prevention into routine diabetes care.

stories.title: KGMU launches program to reduce neonatal deaths
stories.summary: KGMU has launched an ICMR-funded program to provide respiratory support and early breastfeeding to critically ill newborns. The project aims to address Uttar Pradesh's neonatal mortality rate of 28 deaths per 1,000 live births, which remains higher than the national average of 19.

stories.title: President inaugurates malaria research institute jubilee
stories.summary: President Droupadi Murmu inaugurated the golden jubilee celebrations of the ICMR-National Institute of Malaria Research. The President noted that malaria has historically been one of India's most significant public health challenges, particularly for rural and tribal communities, and recognized the contributions of researchers and healthcare workers.

stories.title: Thiamine Deficiency Re-Emerges Among Pregnant, Lactating Women In Parts Of Northeast: ICMR-NIN Study - NDTV
Government health spending triples over decade
stories.summary: Government health spending reached Rs 4.14 lakh crore between 2013-14 and 2023-24, according to the Health Ministry. Public funding increased more than three times, while the proportion of out-of-pocket household expenses fell from 64.2 per cent to 42.7 per cent over the same period.

stories.title: Ayushman Bharat crosses 11.69 crore hospital admissions, 6.74 crore in private hospitals: Govt - DD News
Centre proposes restricting treatment packages to govt hospitals
stories.summary: The Centre has proposed reserving 112 treatment packages under Ayushman Bharat exclusively for government hospitals starting December 1. The move would add 89 packages to the 23 already restricted, potentially limiting where beneficiaries can receive care for these specific procedures.

stories.title: FSSAI questions Red Bull marketing
stories.summary: The FSSAI has asked Red Bull India to provide scientific evidence for marketing its beverage as an energy drink. The regulator observed that the drink derives a significant proportion of its energy content from added sugar and caffeine. It is also considering a ban on the label.

stories.title: FSSAI suspends licenses of six nutraceutical firms
stories.summary: The FSSAI has initiated regulatory action against six nutraceutical manufacturers, including Airen Herbals and Vedant Remedies, for serious food safety violations. The regulator confirmed the suspension of licenses for the companies in a social media post on Monday. The list of violations remains under review.

stories.title: ICMR-NIN reports thiamine deficiency in expectant mothers
stories.summary: A survey by the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition found significant vitamin B1 shortages among expectant mothers in Assam and Tripura. The study analyzed 1,083 women across 120 villages in regions with a history of beriberi. Experts are now urging clinicians to increase vigilance during routine antenatal checkups.

stories.title: Study finds chemical cocktail in Delhi's Yamuna
stories.summary: Researchers from the University of Delhi identified microplastics alongside a mixture of pharmaceutical residues, pesticides, and industrial effluents in the Yamuna river. The study, published in September 2026, analyzed pollution profiles across a 48.8-km stretch of the river. Many of these substances are classified as health hazards.

stories.title: Analysis links air pollution to broad health impacts
stories.summary: An analysis of over 180 epidemiological studies published between 1975 and 2025 found that 91 percent linked air pollution to adverse health effects. Impacts cited include cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and pregnancy complications. The report was released by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air.

stories.title: AIIMS proposes national poisoning registry
stories.summary: AIIMS New Delhi has proposed a unified National Poisoning Registry to modernize acute poison surveillance. The initiative aims to link healthcare facilities nationwide to provide emergency physicians with real-time data. Currently, clinicians manage toxicological emergencies without a central tracking mechanism to guide their treatment efforts.

stories.title: US loses measles elimination status
stories.summary: Global health authorities have announced that the US lost its measles elimination status after 26 years. The country is currently experiencing its worst outbreak since 1991, with over 5,400 cases and eight deaths recorded in 2026. Measles is now considered endemic in the United States.

stories.title: US loses measles elimination status, major setback for US public health to video
stories.summary: US loses measles elimination status, major setback for US public health to video The US lost its measles elimination status, global health authorities have announced on Tuesday, an official recognition that the infectious disease is endemic in the US after being declared eliminated for 26 years. The announcement comes as

stories.title: Measles is no longer considered eliminated in the US and Mexico
stories.summary: The U.S. has lost its measles-free status, international health officials said Tuesday, as the highly contagious virus once relegated to medical textbooks has spread,largely among the unvaccinated,at the highest rate in more than 30 years.

stories.title: U.S. loses measles elimination status, marking embarrassing stain on its public health record
stories.summary: International health officials said Tuesday that measles is no longer considered eliminated in the United States, a finding that was widely expected but that marks an embarrassing and avoidable backslide in the country’s basic public health standing. The announcement, made after a meeting of a committee of the Pan American

stories.title: U.S. loses measles-free status after continued spread of the disease: report
stories.summary: The Pan American Health Organization has revoked the United States’ measles-elimination status after 26 years, because the country did not halt continuous transmission of the highly contagious virus for more than a year, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday (November 13, 2026). The international health body did not immediately

stories.title: WHO urges implementation of antimicrobial resistance plans
stories.summary: New survey data from the World Health Organization shows that while most countries have developed plans to address antimicrobial resistance, few have provided the necessary financing. The organization is calling for nations to move from drafting policy to implementing funded programs.

stories.title: Global antimicrobial resistance efforts remain underfunded
stories.summary: The World Health Organization reports that 173 of 183 surveyed countries have national action plans to tackle antimicrobial resistance, up from 79 in 2017. However, only 42 countries have actually financed and implemented these plans. The world remains off pace to meet key 2030 targets.

stories.title: Ebola outbreak in DRC continues to accelerate
stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo remains out of control six months after its declaration. Infections and deaths are rising at double the rate of the 2014-16 West Africa crisis. Resource shortages and attacks on health workers continue to hamper containment efforts.

stories.title: Congo’s Ebola outbreak is spreading and killing at a record pace
stories.summary: By Jessica Donati DAKAR, Nov 16 (Reuters) - The Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo remains out of control six months after it was first declared, with case numbers and deaths still rising at a record pace. Despite an outpouring of aid, resource shortages, insecurity and poor coordination

stories.title: Explainer: Congo’s Ebola outbreak is spreading and killing at a record pace
stories.summary: Congo’s Ebola outbreak is still spreading six months after it began, with over 11,000 infections and more than 5,500 deaths, making it the second-largest on record. - The rare Bundibugyo strain is moving faster than past outbreaks, and official data says cases and deaths are rising at twice the pace

stories.title: WHO warns of rising respiratory illness in Gaza
stories.summary: The World Health Organization warned of surging respiratory infections in Gaza, noting 33,000 more cases than at this time last year. Overcrowding and poor living conditions are expected to worsen as winter rains flood tent settlements. The organization expects the situation to deteriorate further.

stories.title: Gaza health ministry: Restrictions on patient evacuations threaten thousands of critical cases - وكالة سبأ
BMJ Digital Health and Google Cloud partner on AI
stories.summary: BMJ Digital Health is a launch partner for Google Cloud's Gemini for healthcare. The collaboration aims to combine clinical decision support with longitudinal health records to deliver insights at the point of care. The goal is to make AI-generated healthcare insights more meaningful and reliable for clinicians.

stories.title: AI approach targets sepsis deaths in emergency departments
stories.summary: A new AI approach aims to explain the causes behind patient deaths. By identifying these factors, researchers hope to provide hospital managers with the data needed to implement targeted changes in emergency department operations.

stories.title: CureMetrix wins 2026 Rising Star award
stories.summary: CureMetrix received the 2026 Rising Star award at the Digital Health and AI Awards. The company was selected from more than 1,300 participating firms following a multi-stage evaluation. The recognition highlights its work in advancing the clinical value of routine mammography through AI-driven insights.

stories.title: UK firms prepare to challenge Palantir for NHS FDP contract - Home | Digital Health
Healthcare startups showcase tech at INVEST conference
stories.summary: The INVEST Digital Health conference in Dallas featured startups focused on direct-to-consumer diagnostics and drug platforms. Companies shared technologies intended to remedy industry challenges, including the difficulty of identifying which oncology patients will benefit most from specific drug treatments.

stories.title: AIIMS Nagpur and IIIT Pune sign research partnership
stories.summary: AIIMS Nagpur and IIIT Pune have signed a memorandum of understanding to collaborate on medical data analytics, healthcare informatics, and AI-based diagnosis. The partnership will utilize shared labs and data to explore technology-driven approaches to clinical expertise and engineering.

stories.title: $15M for preventive health tech in India and more briefs - MobiHealthNews
Indonesia to regulate digital health platforms
stories.summary: The Indonesian Health Ministry plans to regulate all digital healthcare platforms, including telemedicine, medical records management, and service pricing. These upcoming regulations aim to ensure that digital innovations operate safely, transparently, and accountably across the country's health technology ecosystem.

stories.title: Reimbursement is now a product decision in digital health - Fast Company
Vietnam - Sweden promote digital health and precision medicine cooperation - Laodong.vn
Indonesia launches inclusive digital health guidelines
stories.summary: Indonesia has introduced new guidelines to make digital health services more accessible to underserved groups, including people with disabilities, the elderly, women, and children. The initiative aims to help electronic system providers improve the inclusivity of their digital health offerings.

stories.title: Happiest Health announces digital business unit
stories.summary: Happiest Health has launched a fifth business unit, Happiest Digital Health, with a roadmap of 11 applications. The company has committed 500 crore rupees to technology investment to extend its care beyond the clinic through an integrated digital approach.

stories.title: Study links irregular sleep to mental health symptoms
stories.summary: Researchers analyzing wearable data from 23,000 adults found that irregular sleep patterns are associated with more severe symptoms of depression and anxiety. The study suggests that maintaining consistent sleep hours may be a significant habit for mental health that requires no additional time.

stories.title: Weekly park visits linked to child development
stories.summary: A study of 4,219 children suggests that visiting parks at least once a week is associated with better social-emotional development. Researchers indicate that outdoor play could be a simple method for supporting children's mental health and social skills as they grow.

stories.title: Mental health curriculum shows benefits in German schools
stories.summary: Secondary school students in Hesse, Germany, who participated in an adapted mental health curriculum showed greater gains in literacy and reduced personal stigma compared to peers. The study evaluated the effectiveness of the program under real-world educational conditions.

stories.title: Review identifies youth mental health priorities
stories.summary: A scoping review in Nova Scotia has identified five policy recommendations to integrate child and youth mental health into climate adaptation strategies. The study aimed to co-develop actionable guidance by engaging local mental health advocates, climate experts, and public sector leaders.

stories.title: Employment instability linked to long-term mental health
stories.summary: Longitudinal data from Australia indicates that chronic employment instability between ages 18 and 24 is associated with poorer mental health outcomes at ages 25 and 35. The findings suggest that early career experiences serve as an influential determinant of long-term wellbeing.

stories.title: Study explores sleep consistency and mental health
stories.summary: A study of nearly 23,000 adults using Oura Rings tracked how daily shifts in sleep timing relate to depression, anxiety, and loneliness. The research moves beyond total sleep duration to examine how irregular schedules might impact mental health symptoms.

stories.title: Mature happiness linked to better mental health outcomes
stories.summary: A 2021 study of 12,203 people across 30 countries suggests calm mature happiness predicts mental health better than standard well-being models. The authors propose fructification, an untested concept of turning personal growth into good for others. Cheerfulness gets plenty of credit, but a quieter state of mind may do more.

stories.title: Karnataka High Court orders review of police mental health policies
stories.summary: The High Court of Karnataka has advised security and police organisations to review mental health policies for personnel carrying firearms. The order followed the quashing of criminal proceedings against a sub-inspector who attempted suicide. Authorities are now asked to strengthen welfare measures for those on duty.

stories.title: Study finds link between cats and child mental health issues
stories.summary: Researchers in Spain are investigating the emotional bond between children and their pets. A recent study identifies cats as the only pet linked to increased mental health problems in children. The findings arrive as pet ownership rates in the country continue to rise.

stories.title: Smartphone use linked to youth distress in comparative study
stories.summary: A study published in the Journal of Activity, Sedentary and Sleep Behaviors found that problematic smartphone use correlates with higher psychological distress in children and adolescents. Data from Canada and Algeria indicate that increased device engagement tracks with elevated symptoms of depression, anxiety, and stress.

stories.title: Cannabis addiction linked to higher odds of suicidal thoughts
stories.summary: A study of more than 415,000 Americans found that adults with cannabis use disorder face 57 percent higher odds of experiencing suicidal thoughts. The risk is particularly elevated among women and younger adults. Researchers are investigating these mental health effects as marijuana availability increases.

stories.title: Air pollution linked to poor mental health in six-state study
stories.summary: A 2023 macroanalysis published in The Journal of Development Studies identified a causal link between worsening air pollution and poor mental health. The study, which tracked 21,203 individuals across six states, suggests that seasonal smog levels provide a critical window for clinical mental health screening.

research.title: Ozempic and Mounjaro may have a surprising effect on your brain
research.summary: Blockbuster weight loss drugs like Ozempic and Mounjaro may do more than help people shed pounds, with growing evidence suggesting they could also influence brain health. Although studies have linked GLP-1 medications to a lower risk of dementia, major trials found that semaglutide did not slow Alzheimer's disease.
